questions.q: Customers who owe money to the business for goods sold to them on credit are called ______.
questions.e: Debtors (trade receivables) are persons who owe an amount to the business; they are shown as current assets.

questions.q: Cash or goods withdrawn by the owner from the business for personal use is called ______.
questions.e: Drawings reduce the owner's capital and are not a business expense.

questions.q: The art of recording financial transactions in the books of account in a systematic manner is called ______.
questions.e: Book keeping is the recording phase; accounting goes further to classify, summarise, analyse and communicate the information.

questions.q: Assets such as land, building and machinery held for long-term use in the business, and not for resale, are called ______ assets.
questions.e: Fixed (non-current) assets are used to carry on the business over many years and are not meant for sale.

questions.q: Riya started a business with ₹2,00,000. During the year she earned a profit of ₹50,000 and withdrew ₹20,000 for personal use. What is her closing capital (in ₹)?
The assumption that a business will continue to operate for a long period and will not be closed in the foreseeable future is the ______ concept.
questions.e: Because of the going concern concept, fixed assets are recorded at cost and depreciated over their useful life.

questions.q: Recording an asset at the price paid to acquire it, and not at its market value, follows the ______ concept.
questions.e: Under the historical cost concept, assets are recorded at acquisition cost, which is objective and verifiable.

questions.q: 'Anticipate no profit but provide for all possible losses' is the essence of the concept of ______.
questions.e: Prudence (conservatism) is why closing stock is valued at cost or net realisable value, whichever is lower.

questions.q: The basis of accounting in which revenues and expenses are recorded when they are earned or incurred, irrespective of receipt or payment of cash, is the ______ basis.
questions.e: Under the accrual basis, outstanding expenses and accrued incomes are also taken into account.

questions.q: Mohan pays his household electricity bill out of business cash, and it is treated as his drawings. Which accounting concept requires this treatment?
questions.e: Under the business entity concept, the owner and the business are separate, so personal expenses paid by the business are drawings.

questions.q: A firm buys a stapler costing ₹50 that will last for 3 years, but charges the whole amount as an expense of the current year instead of treating it as an asset. Which accounting concept justifies this?
questions.e: Items of insignificant amount need not be treated strictly; materiality allows a small capital item to be expensed.

questions.q: The book in which transactions are first recorded in chronological order is called the ______.
questions.e: The journal is the book of original entry; entries are later posted to the ledger.

questions.q: Accounts of individuals, firms and companies, such as Ramesh's account or Bank account, are classified as ______ accounts.
questions.e: Under the traditional classification, accounts of persons (natural or artificial) are personal accounts.

questions.q: The owner withdrew goods costing ₹5,000 from the business for personal use. Which account is credited in the journal entry?
questions.e: Entry: Drawings A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c, because goods withdrawn reduce the goods purchased for sale.

questions.q: Cash ₹10,000 was paid to Sohan, a supplier (creditor). Which account is debited?
questions.e: Entry: Sohan A/c Dr. To Cash A/c; the creditor's liability decreases, so his account is debited.

questions.q: The process of transferring entries from the journal to the respective ledger accounts is called ______.
questions.e: Posting classifies transactions account-wise in the ledger, the principal book of accounts.

questions.q: The total assets of a business are ₹5,00,000 and its outside liabilities are ₹1,80,000. Using the accounting equation, find the owner's capital (in ₹).
questions.e: Capital = Assets - Liabilities = 5,00,000 - 1,80,000 = ₹3,20,000.

questions.q: Goods with a list price of ₹20,000 were sold to Arjun at a trade discount of 10% and a cash discount of 2% for immediate payment. Arjun paid immediately. How much cash (in ₹) was received?
questions.e: Invoice value = 20,000 - 10% = ₹18,000; cash discount = 2% of 18,000 = ₹360; cash received = ₹17,640.

questions.q: Meera, a trader in Jaipur, purchased goods for ₹40,000 on credit from Sohan of Jaipur (intra-state). GST is 12% (CGST 6% and SGST 6%).
p: (a) What is the amount of CGST (in ₹)?
(b) What is the total amount payable to Sohan (in ₹)?
(c) Which account is credited in the journal entry?
Sohan|Sohan's account|Sohan a/c|Sohan account
questions.e: CGST = SGST = 6% of 40,000 = ₹2,400 each; total = 40,000 + 4,800 = ₹44,800, credited to Sohan's account as the creditor.

questions.q: The special book in which all cash receipts and cash payments are recorded is the ______.
questions.e: The cash book is both a book of original entry and a ledger account for cash.

questions.q: Goods returned by customers are recorded in the ______ book.
questions.a: sales return|sales returns|return inwards|returns inward|sales returns book
questions.e: Sales returns (return inwards) book records goods returned by customers, usually supported by a credit note issued.

questions.q: An entry that appears on both the debit and credit sides of a double column cash book, such as cash deposited into bank, is called a ______ entry.
questions.e: Contra entries affect both cash and bank columns and are marked with C for not posting to the ledger.

questions.q: Credit purchases of goods meant for resale are recorded in the ______ book.
questions.e: The purchases book records only credit purchases of goods; cash purchases go to the cash book.

questions.q: Under the imprest system, the petty cashier was given ₹5,000 at the start of the week and spent ₹3,650 during the week. How much (in ₹) will the head cashier give him at the start of the next week?
questions.e: Under the imprest system, the amount spent is reimbursed so that the petty cash is restored to ₹5,000.

questions.q: A statement prepared to reconcile the balance as per the cash book with the balance as per the pass book is called a ______.
questions.e: A BRS explains the causes of difference between the bank column of the cash book and the pass book on a date.

questions.q: A debit balance as per the pass book indicates a bank ______.
questions.e: In the bank's books, a debit balance means the customer owes the bank, i.e. an overdraft.

questions.q: Balance as per cash book is ₹15,000 (debit). Cheques of ₹4,000 issued have not been presented for payment, and bank charges of ₹200 are not recorded in the cash book. Find the balance as per pass book (in ₹).
questions.e: Pass book balance = 15,000 + 4,000 (unpresented cheques) - 200 (bank charges) = ₹18,800.

questions.q: The pass book shows a credit balance of ₹25,000. Cheques of ₹6,000 deposited have not yet been credited by the bank, and interest of ₹500 credited by the bank is not recorded in the cash book. Find the balance as per cash book (in ₹).
questions.e: Cash book balance = 25,000 + 6,000 (uncleared cheques) - 500 (interest not in cash book) = ₹30,500.

questions.q: On 31 March, Arjun's cash book shows a debit bank balance of ₹50,000. Cheques of ₹8,000 deposited were not collected by the bank, and a customer deposited ₹3,000 directly into the bank, which is not recorded in the cash book.
p: (a) Because of the uncollected cheques alone, will the pass book balance be higher or lower than the cash book balance?
lower
(b) What is the balance as per pass book (in ₹)?
questions.e: Uncollected cheques make the pass book lower by ₹8,000 and the direct deposit makes it higher by ₹3,000: 50,000 - 8,000 + 3,000 = ₹45,000.

questions.t: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
questions.q: A statement showing the debit and credit balances of all ledger accounts on a particular date is called a ______.
questions.e: A trial balance checks the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger.

questions.t: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
questions.q: When the trial balance does not agree, the difference is temporarily placed in a(n) ______ account.
questions.e: The suspense account is closed when the errors causing the difference are located and rectified.

questions.t: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
questions.q: Wages paid for installation of new machinery were debited to Wages account. This is an error of ______.
questions.e: Capital expenditure treated as revenue expenditure violates accounting principles; it should be debited to Machinery account.

questions.t: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
questions.q: A credit sale to Gopal for ₹5,000 was correctly entered in the sales book but posted to Gopi's account. This is an error of ______.
questions.e: Posting to the wrong account of the right class is an error of commission; it does not affect the trial balance.

questions.t: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
questions.q: Purchase of furniture for ₹10,000 was wrongly debited to Purchases account. In the rectifying entry, which account is debited?
questions.e: Rectifying entry: Furniture A/c Dr. To Purchases A/c ₹10,000.

questions.t: Trial Balance and Rectification of Errors
questions.q: The debit total of a trial balance is ₹2,45,600 and the credit total is ₹2,48,000. What amount (in ₹) will be placed on the debit side of the suspense account?
questions.e: The debit side is short by 2,48,000 - 2,45,600 = ₹2,400, so the suspense account shows a debit balance of ₹2,400.

questions.q: Depreciation is a ______ expense because no cash goes out of the business when it is charged.
questions.e: Depreciation allocates the cost of an asset over its life; no cash outflow occurs when it is charged.

questions.q: A machine costs ₹1,00,000, has a scrap value of ₹10,000 and a useful life of 5 years. Find the annual depreciation (in ₹) under the straight line method.
A reserve created out of profits that is not meant for any specific purpose and strengthens the financial position of the business is a ______ reserve.
questions.e: A general (free) reserve is available for any purpose, unlike a specific reserve such as a dividend equalisation reserve.

questions.q: A machine costing ₹2,00,000 is depreciated at 10% p.a. on the written down value method. Find the depreciation (in ₹) for the second year.
A machine was purchased on 1 October 2023 for ₹80,000. Depreciation is charged at 10% p.a. on the straight line method. Find the depreciation (in ₹) for the year ending 31 March 2024.
questions.e: The machine was used for 6 months: 80,000 × 10% × 6/12 = ₹4,000.

questions.q: Arjun & Co. bought a machine on 1 April 2022 for ₹1,20,000 and spent ₹10,000 on its installation. Depreciation is charged at 10% p.a. on the straight line method (no scrap value). Accounts close on 31 March.
p: (a) What is the annual depreciation (in ₹)?
(b) What is the book value of the machine on 31 March 2024 (in ₹)?
(c) If the machine is sold on 31 March 2024 for ₹1,00,000, what is the loss on sale (in ₹)?
questions.e: Cost = ₹1,30,000 (installation is capitalised); depreciation = ₹13,000 a year; book value after 2 years = ₹1,04,000; loss = 1,04,000 - 1,00,000 = ₹4,000.

questions.q: The account prepared to find the gross profit or gross loss of a business is the ______ account.
questions.e: The trading account compares net sales with the cost of goods sold to find gross profit.

questions.q: Opening stock is ₹20,000, purchases are ₹80,000 and closing stock is ₹30,000. Find the cost of goods sold (in ₹).
questions.e: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock = 20,000 + 80,000 - 30,000 = ₹70,000.

questions.q: Carriage inwards, being a direct expense, is debited to the ______ account.
questions.e: Carriage inwards adds to the cost of purchases, so it goes to the trading account; carriage outwards goes to profit and loss account.

questions.q: Sales are ₹3,00,000, sales returns are ₹20,000 and cost of goods sold is ₹2,10,000. Find the gross profit (in ₹).
Gross profit is ₹1,50,000. Salaries are ₹40,000, rent is ₹24,000, discount allowed is ₹2,000 and interest received is ₹6,000. Find the net profit (in ₹).
Closing stock given as an adjustment outside the trial balance is credited to the trading account and also shown on the assets side of the ______.
questions.e: An adjustment affects two places: closing stock appears in the trading account and as a current asset in the balance sheet.

questions.q: Debtors are ₹50,000. Further bad debts of ₹2,000 are to be written off and a provision for doubtful debts is to be created at 5% on debtors. Find the amount of the provision (in ₹).
questions.e: Provision is made on good debtors: 5% of (50,000 - 2,000) = ₹2,400.

questions.q: The trial balance of Meera Traders on 31 March 2024 shows Insurance ₹12,000 paid for the year ending 30 June 2024 and Salaries ₹55,000. Salaries of ₹5,000 are outstanding.
p: (a) What is the amount of prepaid insurance (in ₹)?
(b) What amount of salaries (in ₹) will be debited to the profit and loss account?
(c) Outstanding salaries are shown in the balance sheet as a current ______.
liability|liabilities
questions.e: Insurance for April-June 2024 (3 months) = 12,000 × 3/12 = ₹3,000 prepaid; salaries = 55,000 + 5,000 = ₹60,000; outstanding expenses are current liabilities.

questions.q: Commission received of ₹18,000 includes ₹3,000 received in advance. Interest of ₹1,500 has accrued but not been received.
p: (a) What amount of commission (in ₹) will be credited to the profit and loss account?
(b) Accrued interest is shown in the balance sheet as a current ______.
asset|assets
(c) What is the total income (in ₹) from these two items credited to the profit and loss account?
questions.e: Commission earned = 18,000 - 3,000 = ₹15,000; accrued interest is income of the year and a current asset; total = 15,000 + 1,500 = ₹16,500.

questions.q: In the absence of a partnership deed, partners share profits and losses ______.
questions.e: Under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, if there is no deed, profits and losses are shared equally.

questions.q: In the absence of a partnership deed, interest on a partner's loan to the firm is allowed at ______% per annum.
questions.e: Section 13 of the Partnership Act provides interest at 6% p.a. on partners' loans when there is no agreement.

questions.q: As per the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014, what is the maximum number of partners allowed in a partnership firm?
questions.e: The Companies Act, 2013 allows the number to be prescribed up to 100; the 2014 Rules fix it at 50.

questions.q: Under the fixed capital method, interest on capital, salary, share of profit and drawings are recorded in partners' ______ accounts.
questions.e: Under the fixed capital method, capital accounts show only capital introduced or withdrawn; all other adjustments go to current accounts.

questions.q: Amit withdrew ₹2,000 at the beginning of every month during the year ended 31 March 2024. Calculate interest on drawings (in ₹) at 6% p.a.
questions.e: Total drawings = ₹24,000; for beginning-of-month drawings the average period is 6.5 months: 24,000 × 6/100 × 6.5/12 = ₹780.

questions.q: Meera's capital on 1 April 2023 was ₹3,00,000. She introduced additional capital of ₹1,00,000 on 1 October 2023. Calculate interest on capital (in ₹) at 10% p.a. for the year ended 31 March 2024.
Ravi and Sohan share profits in the ratio 3:2. Their capitals are ₹2,00,000 and ₹1,00,000. The deed allows interest on capital at 5% p.a. The net profit before interest is ₹60,000.
p: (a) What is Ravi's interest on capital (in ₹)?
(b) What is the divisible profit after interest on capital (in ₹)?
(c) What is Sohan's share of the divisible profit (in ₹)?
questions.e: Interest: Ravi ₹10,000, Sohan ₹5,000; divisible profit = 60,000 - 15,000 = ₹45,000; Sohan gets 2/5 of 45,000 = ₹18,000.

questions.q: Goodwill is a(n) ______ asset because it cannot be seen or touched.
questions.e: Goodwill is an intangible but not a fictitious asset; it has a realisable value when the business is sold.

questions.q: The average profit of a firm is ₹50,000. Calculate goodwill (in ₹) at 3 years' purchase of average profit.
questions.e: Goodwill = Average profit × Number of years' purchase = 50,000 × 3 = ₹1,50,000.

questions.q: Capital employed is ₹5,00,000, the normal rate of return is 10% and the average profit is ₹80,000. Calculate goodwill (in ₹) at 3 years' purchase of super profit.
The super profit of a firm is ₹24,000 and the normal rate of return is 12%. Calculate goodwill (in ₹) by the capitalisation of super profit method.
questions.e: Goodwill = Super profit × 100 ÷ Normal rate of return = 24,000 × 100/12 = ₹2,00,000.

questions.q: The ratio in which partners agree to give up their share of profit in favour of another partner is called the ______ ratio.
questions.e: Sacrificing ratio = Old ratio - New ratio.

questions.q: Gaining ratio is calculated as: New ratio minus ______ ratio.
questions.e: A partner whose new share exceeds his old share gains; gaining ratio = new ratio - old ratio.

questions.q: A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. They decide to share profits equally in future. Which partner gains?
questions.e: B's share rises from 2/5 to 1/2, a gain of 1/10, while A sacrifices 1/10.

questions.q: X and Y share profits in the ratio 3:2 and decide to share equally in future. Goodwill of the firm is valued at ₹1,00,000. What amount (in ₹) will be debited to Y's capital account for the adjustment of goodwill?
questions.e: Y gains 1/2 - 2/5 = 1/10; Y's capital is debited with 1/10 × 1,00,000 = ₹10,000 and X's capital is credited.

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 3:1 and decide to share equally from 1 April 2024. A General Reserve of ₹60,000 appears in the books, and they decide not to distribute it but to pass an adjustment entry.
p: (a) Which partner is the gaining partner?
Q|partner Q
(b) What amount (in ₹) will be debited to the gaining partner's capital account?
questions.e: P's share falls from 3/4 to 1/2 (sacrifice 1/4) and Q's rises from 1/4 to 1/2 (gain 1/4); Q's capital is debited with 1/4 × 60,000 = ₹15,000.

questions.q: The amount brought in by a new partner in cash for his share of goodwill is called ______.
questions.e: Premium for goodwill compensates the old partners for the share of profit they sacrifice.

questions.q: At the time of admission, an increase in the value of assets is credited to ______ account.
questions.e: Gains and losses on revaluation of assets and liabilities go to the Revaluation Account and are shared by old partners in the old ratio.

questions.q: C is admitted into a firm for a 1/4 share in profits and brings ₹40,000 as his capital. What is the total capital (in ₹) of the new firm implied by C's contribution?
questions.e: Implied total capital = 40,000 × 4/1 = ₹1,60,000.

questions.q: D is admitted for a 1/4 share and brings ₹60,000 as capital. The adjusted capitals of the old partners A and B total ₹1,50,000. Calculate the hidden goodwill of the firm (in ₹).
questions.e: Implied total capital = 60,000 × 4 = ₹2,40,000; actual capital = 1,50,000 + 60,000 = ₹2,10,000; hidden goodwill = ₹30,000.

questions.q: A and B share profits in the ratio 3:2. On admission of C, stock is increased by ₹10,000, a provision for doubtful debts of ₹4,000 is created and building is appreciated by ₹15,000.
p: (a) What is the profit on revaluation (in ₹)?
(b) What is A's share of revaluation profit (in ₹)?
(c) What is B's share of revaluation profit (in ₹)?
questions.e: Revaluation profit = 10,000 + 15,000 - 4,000 = ₹21,000, shared by old partners 3:2 as ₹12,600 and ₹8,400.

questions.t: Retirement and Death of a Partner
questions.q: The ratio in which the continuing partners acquire the share of a retiring partner is called the ______ ratio.
questions.e: Continuing partners compensate the retiring partner for goodwill in their gaining ratio.

questions.t: Retirement and Death of a Partner
questions.q: If the amount due to a retiring partner is not paid immediately, it is transferred to his ______ account.
questions.e: The unpaid balance becomes a liability of the firm and is shown as the retiring partner's loan.

questions.t: Retirement and Death of a Partner
questions.q: A partner with a 1/4 share died 3 months after the beginning of the accounting year. Last year's profit was ₹1,20,000. Calculate his share of profit (in ₹) till the date of death on the basis of last year's profit.
questions.e: Share = 1,20,000 × 3/12 × 1/4 = ₹7,500, debited to Profit and Loss Suspense Account.

questions.t: Retirement and Death of a Partner
questions.q: X, Y and Z are partners. Z retires and his share of goodwill of ₹18,000 is adjusted through the capital accounts of X and Y, who gain in the ratio 3:2. What amount (in ₹) is debited to X's capital account?
questions.e: X's share = 18,000 × 3/5 = ₹10,800; Y bears ₹7,200; Z's capital is credited with ₹18,000.

questions.q: On dissolution of a firm, all assets (other than cash) and outside liabilities are transferred to ______ account.
questions.e: The Realisation Account records the sale of assets and payment of liabilities and finds the profit or loss on realisation.

questions.q: On dissolution, as per Section 48, a partner's loan to the firm is paid ______ the partners' capitals are paid.
questions.e: Outside liabilities are paid first, then partners' loans, and lastly partners' capitals.

questions.q: On dissolution, assets (other than cash) of book value ₹2,00,000 realised ₹1,70,000; creditors of ₹50,000 were paid ₹48,000; realisation expenses were ₹3,000. Calculate the loss on realisation (in ₹).
questions.e: Loss on assets ₹30,000, gain on creditors ₹2,000, expenses ₹3,000: net loss = 30,000 - 2,000 + 3,000 = ₹31,000.

questions.q: Ravi and Meera dissolve their firm. Creditors of ₹40,000 are paid at a discount of 5%. An unrecorded computer worth ₹5,000 is taken over by Ravi.
p: (a) How much cash (in ₹) is paid to the creditors?
(b) Which account is debited for the payment to creditors?
realisation|realisation account|realization|realisation a/c
(c) Which account is credited when Ravi takes over the unrecorded computer?
realisation|realisation account|realization|realisation a/c
questions.e: Creditors get 40,000 - 5% = ₹38,000 (Realisation A/c Dr. To Cash); an unrecorded asset taken by a partner is entered as Ravi's Capital A/c Dr. To Realisation A/c.

questions.q: When shares are issued at a price higher than their face value, they are said to be issued at a ______.
questions.e: The excess over face value is credited to the Securities Premium Account.

questions.q: The part of uncalled capital that a company resolves to call up only in the event of its winding up is called ______ capital.
questions.e: Reserve capital is available only to creditors on winding up and cannot be called up earlier.

questions.q: In the balance sheet of a company, Securities Premium is shown under the heading Reserves and ______.
questions.e: As per Schedule III, Securities Premium appears under Shareholders' Funds - Reserves and Surplus.

questions.q: A company issued 10,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a premium of ₹2 per share. What amount (in ₹) is credited to Securities Premium?
questions.e: Securities premium = 10,000 × ₹2 = ₹20,000; share capital is credited with ₹1,00,000.

questions.q: A company forfeited 200 equity shares of ₹10 each, ₹8 called up, on which the shareholder had paid ₹5 per share. What amount (in ₹) is credited to Share Forfeiture Account?
questions.e: Share forfeiture is credited with the amount actually received: 200 × ₹5 = ₹1,000.

questions.q: 100 shares of ₹10 each (fully called up), on which ₹6 per share had been paid, were forfeited. They were reissued at ₹8 per share as fully paid. What amount (in ₹) is transferred to Capital Reserve?
questions.e: Forfeited amount = 100 × 6 = ₹600; discount on reissue = 100 × 2 = ₹200; capital reserve = 600 - 200 = ₹400.

questions.q: A company issued 50,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at ₹12 per share, payable ₹3 on application, ₹5 on allotment (including premium) and the balance on calls. Applications were received for 70,000 shares and allotment was made pro-rata to all applicants; excess application money was adjusted towards allotment.
p: (a) How much application money (in ₹) was received?
(b) How much excess application money (in ₹) was adjusted towards allotment?
(c) How much cash (in ₹) was received on allotment?
questions.e: Application money = 70,000 × 3 = ₹2,10,000; needed for 50,000 shares = ₹1,50,000, so ₹60,000 is excess; allotment due = 50,000 × 5 = ₹2,50,000, so cash received = ₹1,90,000.

questions.q: A debenture holder is a ______ of the company and not its owner.
questions.e: Debentures are borrowed funds; debenture holders get fixed interest and are creditors of the company.

questions.q: Calculate the annual interest (in ₹) on 9% debentures of ₹5,00,000.
questions.e: Interest = 9% of 5,00,000 = ₹45,000, payable even if the company makes a loss.

questions.q: Debentures given to a lender as additional security, besides a principal security, are called debentures issued as collateral ______.
questions.e: Collateral debentures are an additional security; no interest is paid on them as interest is paid on the actual loan.

questions.q: 1,000 debentures of ₹100 each were issued at a discount of 5% and are redeemable at a premium of 10%. What is the loss on issue of debentures (in ₹)?
questions.e: Loss on issue = discount 1,000 × 5 + premium on redemption 1,000 × 10 = 5,000 + 10,000 = ₹15,000.

questions.q: A statement in which each item is expressed as a percentage of a common base, such as revenue from operations or total assets, is called a ______ statement.
questions.e: Common-size statements show the relationship of each item to a common base, aiding vertical analysis.

questions.q: As per Schedule III of the Companies Act, 2013, trade payables due within 12 months are shown under the head ______ liabilities.
questions.e: Trade payables, short-term borrowings and short-term provisions are current liabilities.

questions.q: Revenue from operations is ₹5,00,000 and cost of materials consumed is ₹3,00,000. In a common-size statement of profit and loss, what percentage of revenue is the cost of materials consumed?
Current ratio = Current assets ÷ ______.
questions.e: Current ratio measures short-term solvency; an ideal ratio is often taken as 2:1.

questions.q: Current assets are ₹3,00,000 and current liabilities are ₹1,50,000. Calculate the current ratio.
The current ratio of a company is 2.5:1 and its working capital is ₹60,000. Calculate its current assets (in ₹).
questions.e: Working capital = CA - CL = 2.5 CL - CL = 1.5 CL = 60,000, so CL = ₹40,000 and CA = ₹1,00,000.

questions.q: Revenue from operations is ₹4,00,000 and gross profit is 25% on revenue. Opening inventory is ₹40,000 and closing inventory is ₹60,000.
p: (a) What is the cost of revenue from operations (in ₹)?
(b) What is the average inventory (in ₹)?
(c) What is the inventory turnover ratio (in times)?
times

questions.q: In a cash flow statement, purchase of machinery is classified as a(n) ______ activity.
questions.e: Acquisition and disposal of long-term assets are investing activities.

questions.q: For a non-financial company, payment of dividend is classified as a(n) ______ activity in the cash flow statement.
questions.e: Dividends paid relate to owners' funds, so they are a financing activity (AS 3).

questions.q: Net profit before tax is ₹80,000, depreciation is ₹10,000, trade receivables increased by ₹15,000 and trade payables increased by ₹5,000. Calculate cash flow from operating activities (in ₹), ignoring tax.
questions.e: 80,000 + 10,000 (depreciation) - 15,000 (increase in receivables) + 5,000 (increase in payables) = ₹80,000.
